- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.20), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 7–14 days.
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (days 1–7); apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average for next 10 days.
- When sentiment spikes to 0.33+ and model forecasts rise sharply, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.
